plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders and values uniform on [0,49]. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do—it doesn't depend on beliefs about opponents' bidding functions. Bidding above value risks winning at a loss; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $46, I should bid exactly $46 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of beliefs about opponents' bidding behavior. Since payment is determined by the second-highest bid, overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit in this format. My value is $17, so I will bid exactly that amount.

In a second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values, bidding one's true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This holds because deviating from truthful bidding either loses value when winning or forgoes profitable wins. Since my value is $28, I will bid exactly that amount, ensuring optimal expected profit regardless of competitors' behavior.
